title: Authentication, OAuth and Account
case_ids_frozen_by: P15 contract-freeze revision; Master Plan supplies requirements, not P15-Txxx identifiers

inherited_authorities: P12 Workspace membership/RBAC where account settings intersect Workspace
P14 Turnstile server-side primitive for shared use
capability_contract.scope: P15 closes customer registration/verification/login/recovery/session/account security and CAP-OAUTH runtime lifecycle. P04 owns the pre-existing Auth shell, P12 retains invitation and Workspace membership authority, P14 retains CAP-MAIL and its contact/ticket Turnstile ownership, P17 retains administrator/role/permission lifecycle, P19 retains final Website/Technical SEO, and release-wide P20-P22 remain later-owned.

inherited_p04_authority.scope: Six-shell authority including the Auth shell is inherited; P15 implements identity/account behavior inside that shell without redefining P04 shell contracts.

route_contract.admin_oauth_surface: ADMIN-OAUTH /admin/platform/oauth — P15 CAP-OAUTH provider runtime/configuration contribution only; settings.manage authorization is consumed, not lifecycle-owned
rules: No legacy auth aliases or silent compatibility routes may be invented.
AUTH-INVITE remains P12-owned and is not evidence of P15 CAP-AUTH completion.
All Auth routes are noindex, outside every sitemap and no-store.
APP-SETTINGS and ADMIN-OAUTH are authenticated private surfaces and no-store/noindex.
UI guards never replace server authentication, tenant or permission checks.
P15 consumes settings.manage on ADMIN-OAUTH without implementing the P17 administrator permission lifecycle.
Formal session authority is server-side; formal auth/session tokens are never persisted in localStorage.
Successful authentication rotates or establishes a fresh server session and does not accept client-asserted identity authority.
Cookie-authenticated unsafe mutations enforce CSRF and allowed Origin policy server-side.
Forgot-password responses are account-enumeration neutral.
Verification, reset, login-email and social handoff grants are opaque, expiry-bound and one-time; replay/reuse fails closed.
Passwords, raw verification/reset codes, session tokens and OAuth tokens are never written to ordinary logs/evidence.
Rate-limit and Turnstile decisions are server-authoritative and occur before protected durable mutation.
Session revocation is checked server-side on subsequent requests and cannot be defeated by stale UI state.
auth_contract.mfa_scope: P15 implements the Master Plan MFA UI contracts on account security surfaces without claiming P17 administrator MFA/permission lifecycle.

rules: OAuth state is unpredictable, server-bound, expiry-bound and one-time; mismatch/replay fails closed before identity mutation.
PKCE is enforced where applicable to the provider flow defined by the implementation contract.
Redirect URI is selected from reviewed server configuration and is never accepted as arbitrary client authority.
Provider callback errors expose allowlisted categories only; raw callback parameters, codes, access tokens and provider secrets are excluded from logs/evidence.
The browser callback exchanges provider result for a short-lived opaque handoff; provider credentials are not placed into browser storage.
Social registration cannot silently bind an existing account from an unverified provider/email claim.
Connected-account bind/unbind requires current authenticated account authority and must not reassign an external identity already bound elsewhere.
Provider client secrets are masked in Admin UI and never included in frontend bundles or ordinary evidence.
P15 verification/recovery/login-code delivery reuses P14 durable mail queue/template/mailworker authority; no parallel SMTP path is introduced.
Mail delivery success never proves authentication or token consumption; token state remains server-authoritative.
P15 may add auth-owned allowlisted template keys/variables but cannot weaken P14 secret redaction, idempotency or retry behavior.
P15 auth Turnstile scenarios reuse a server-side verifier/anti-replay boundary and production bypass is prohibited.
P14 contact/ticket Turnstile ownership is not reinterpreted by P15.
Use Design System exact tokens/components; Auth control sizing and form/error/focus behavior are not locally redefined.
Browser evidence covers canonical desktop/tablet/mobile plus 320 CSS px reflow where applicable, keyboard/focus/name-role-value and reduced motion.
Password/payment/OAuth/API secret fields do not use unsafe browser autosave storage; OTP/code input supports correct autocomplete/password-manager semantics and whole-code paste where applicable.
Persistent security/recovery errors are in-page and never toast-only or color-only.
Direct URL loads and API calls repeat server authorization; stale client state cannot present a revoked session as authoritative success.

environment_contract.mysql: Real MySQL 8.x for users, credentials, verification/recovery grants, sessions, OAuth identities/configuration and audit evidence.
environment_contract.redis: Real Redis where P15 uses rate/replay/session coordination; durable identity authority remains server-side.
environment_contract.mailworker: Reuse real native P14 services/platformapi/cmd/mailworker for P15 email delivery evidence.
environment_contract.oauth: CI uses deterministic local provider adapters/protocol fixtures with real state/handoff logic; live production provider secrets are prohibited.
environment_contract.turnstile: Deterministic server-side verifier adapter in CI; production bypass prohibited.
environment_contract.browser: Built Auth/Workspace/Admin surfaces with real local APIs.

closure.scope_rule: P15 closes CAP-AUTH, CAP-OAUTH and only its auth-facing CAP-TURNSTILE contribution. P04/P12/P14/P17/P19 and later release-wide authorities remain separately owned.

cases.name: Identity/session schema and correlation integrity
cases.oracle: Durable user/credential/session/OAuth identity records use server-authoritative state, safe identifiers and correlation without storing raw secrets in evidence.

cases.name: Registration and verification-code issuance
cases.oracle: Registration validates input, issues an expiry-bound one-time verification grant and queues mail through inherited P14 mail authority without duplicate durable accounts.

cases.name: Email verification expiry and replay
cases.oracle: Valid verification succeeds once; invalid, expired and reused grants fail closed without revealing raw token material.

cases.name: Password login authority and account states
cases.oracle: Login is server-authoritative and correctly handles invalid, locked and verification-required states without client identity bypass.

cases.name: Login email-code lifecycle
cases.oracle: Login email codes are expiry-bound, one-time, rate-limited and delivered through P14 mail authority without raw-code evidence leakage.

cases.name: Forgot-password neutral response
cases.oracle: Existing and non-existing account requests expose response-neutral behavior while only valid internal targets receive a reset grant/mail job.

cases.name: Password reset expiry/reuse and post-reset authority
cases.oracle: Reset grant is opaque/one-time/expiry-bound, reuse fails closed and post-reset session policy is enforced server-side.

cases.name: Session cookie and no-localStorage boundary
cases.oracle: Formal session authority uses reviewed cookie/server state, authenticated responses are no-store and formal auth/session tokens are absent from localStorage/frontend bundles.

cases.name: CSRF fail-closed enforcement
cases.oracle: Cookie-authenticated unsafe mutations reject missing/invalid/replayed CSRF authority before durable state change.

cases.name: Origin policy enforcement
cases.oracle: Disallowed or malformed Origin requests fail closed on applicable unsafe auth/account mutations while allowed same-site requests succeed.

cases.name: Auth Turnstile verification and replay
cases.oracle: Protected auth scenarios verify Turnstile server-side; missing/invalid/expired/replayed/provider-failure cases fail closed before protected durable mutation.

cases.name: Auth rate-limit abuse boundary
cases.oracle: Login/code/register/recovery abuse limits are server-authoritative, safe-keyed and return bounded retry semantics without account enumeration.

cases.name: Session list and revoke
cases.oracle: A user can inspect safe session metadata and revoke an owned session; revoked sessions are rejected server-side on later requests and foreign IDs fail closed.

cases.name: Profile and account-security mutation authority
cases.oracle: Profile/security mutations require the current account session, validation/CSRF/Origin checks and auditable correlation; stale client state is not authority.

cases.name: Connected-account bind and unbind integrity
cases.oracle: Bind/unbind is current-account authorized, state-bound and cannot steal/reassign an external identity already bound to another account.

cases.name: OAuth provider registry and secret masking
cases.oracle: Provider registry is exactly google/facebook/github/qq/wechat/rainbow; enabled/configured state is server-derived and client secrets are masked/absent from bundles/evidence.

cases.name: OAuth start state and redirect URI
cases.oracle: Provider start uses unpredictable expiry-bound state and reviewed redirect configuration; arbitrary client redirect authority is rejected.

cases.name: OAuth callback state/PKCE/redaction
cases.oracle: Callback validates state and PKCE where applicable before identity mutation; mismatch/replay fails closed and callback secrets are redacted.

cases.name: OAuth browser handoff lifecycle
cases.oracle: Callback creates only a short-lived opaque one-time browser handoff; expired/reused handoff fails and provider credentials never become browser storage authority.

cases.name: Social registration missing-email/conflict lifecycle
cases.oracle: Social registration handles missing provider email, email-code verification, account conflict and expired handoff without silent unsafe account binding.

cases.name: OAuth cross-account takeover denial
cases.oracle: Forged, replayed or already-bound provider identities cannot authenticate/bind as a different account and denial does not leak provider secrets.

cases.name: P14 mailworker verification/recovery integration
cases.oracle: Verification/recovery/login-code mail jobs use inherited P14 queue/template/mailworker idempotency/retry authority and mail delivery never substitutes for token consumption.

cases.name: Auth security headers/no-store/noindex/CSP
cases.oracle: Auth HTML/API responses expose the frozen no-store/noindex and testable security-header policy, including CSP expectations, without sensitive cache leakage.

cases.name: Auth route browser authority
cases.oracle: Login/register/verify/forgot/reset/OAuth/social-registration frozen states pass responsive, accessibility, focus/error and secret-storage browser contracts on real local APIs.

cases.name: Workspace account settings browser authority
cases.oracle: Profile/security/sessions/connected-account states pass direct-load authorization, revoke/recovery, responsive and accessibility contracts on real local APIs.

cases.name: Admin OAuth configuration browser authority
cases.oracle: ADMIN-OAUTH configured/incomplete/provider-error/secret-masked/test-result states consume server settings permission without exposing secrets or claiming P17 permission lifecycle.

cases.name: Audit and secret/PII evidence safety
cases.oracle: Security-sensitive auth/account/OAuth mutations are correlated/auditable while passwords, raw codes/tokens, OAuth secrets and unnecessary PII are absent from ordinary logs/evidence.

cases.name: Exact-head evidence coherence
cases.oracle: P15-T001..P15-T027 evidence is exact-head bound, producer-coherent, reviewable and mixed-head/unsafe evidence is rejected.

cases.name: Accountable signed exact-head closure
cases.oracle: Signed exact revision proves P15-T001..P15-T028 PASS, required affected exact-head workflow matrix green, phase=signed, merge_authoritative=true and defects P0/P1/DECISION REQUIRED all zero.
